title: Google Project Zero & DeepMind ‘Big Sleep’ Makes First Autonomous AI Zero-Day Vulnerability Discovery
aiSystem: Big Sleep (Gemini 1.5 Pro + Debugger/Browser Agent Harness — Google Project Zero / DeepMind)
whyItMatters: First real-world previously unknown exploitable zero-day memory-corruption vulnerability (a stack buffer underflow in widely deployed SQLite) discovered autonomously by an AI agent before release.
summary: Announced on November 1, 2024 by Google Project Zero and Google DeepMind (evolving from the Naptime LLM vulnerability-research framework), Big Sleep became the first AI agent to autonomously discover a previously unknown, exploitable memory-safety vulnerability in widely used real-world production software. Equipped with code-navigation tools, Python scripting, and a live debugger to mimic human security researchers, the Gemini-powered agent inspected recent SQLite source commits, hypothesized a subtle edge case in index-column parsing, wrote and executed a triggering SQLite proof-of-concept crash, and confirmed an exploitable stack buffer underflow—reported to SQLite maintainers and patched the same day before ever shipping in a public release.
technicalHighlights: First confirmed real-world zero-day vulnerability (stack buffer underflow in SQLite) autonomously discovered and reproduced with a working crashing PoC by an LLM security agent.
Paired Gemini reasoning with live code-browsing, debugging, and test-harness tools rather than blind fuzzing—finding a bug missed by SQLite’s extensive continuous fuzzers.
Demonstrated immediate defensive impact: reported to SQLite developers and patched prior to official release, inaugurating autonomous AI cyber-defense.
caveats: Found in a pre-release development branch commit rather than a decades-old dormant flaw; autonomous auditing still produced false positives requiring human triage and remained early in scaling to full-codebase auditing.

scoreRationale.foundational: Marked the historic threshold where autonomous AI agents moved from synthetic CTF security benchmarks to finding real-world zero-day vulnerabilities in ubiquitous open-source software.
scoreRationale.ripple: Reshaped global cybersecurity, software-auditing workflows, and frontier AI cyber-capability evaluations across industry and governments.
scoreRationale.verification: Confirmed directly by Google Project Zero and independently verified and patched upstream by the SQLite engineering team with a reproducible crash PoC.
scoreRationale.velocity: Audited live software commits and synthesized a working memory-corruption trigger faster than continuous fuzzing pipelines.

sources.label: Google Project Zero — From Naptime to Big Sleep: Using Large Language Models To Catch Vulnerabilities In Real-World Code (Nov 2024)
